open_questions.question: Built by Claude Code subagents outside the Hub's flows (operator, 2026-10-27), so delivery is none; tasks are closed as already built against the merged commits once their acceptance drives pass.

problem: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'when we reject or an agent rejects an evidence, all evidences are rejected on the same value ... should each evidence behave separately? This way we have a tracing of which evidence were rejected and why ... that is confusing.' Today the task's verdict decides all its awaiting evidence at once (task_transition_service.py:1023 calling requirement_evidence.decide_with_verdict): approving accepts every piece, sending back rejects every piece with the one verdict reason. It was built so no second decision is needed (F672). The cost: QA wrote on slice 1 of the red thread that FR-4, FR-7, FR-8 and FR-12 'held ... but are rejected with this verdict because they come from the same commit'; slice 2 shows 30 of 54 pieces 'rejected', which mostly counts send-backs times requirements (vault src-109565ec0558), so neither the record nor model comparisons say what actually failed.

requirements.statement: A reviewer sending a task back can name the pieces of evidence that fail, each with its own reason, in the same action that sends it back; only the named pieces become rejected, each with its own reason.

requirements.rationale: A piece that held is not wrong; calling it rejected is what made the record and the counts misleading.
requirements.statement: On a send-back, every awaiting piece of the task that the reviewer did not name as failing becomes held at its commit: not rejected, not accepted, and shown as held with the send-back's reason.
A send-back that names no failing piece is allowed when it gives a reason (a defect outside any requirement, a failing check), and then every awaiting piece is held.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26, option B: re-recording is correct by construction; carrying forward waits for slice H's numbers.
requirements.statement: A held piece never counts as accepted evidence; the requirement it served needs a new piece at the builder's next commit, and the reviewer's next verdict judges that new piece.

requirements.rationale: F672: a second decision by someone else stalled finished work.
requirements.statement: Neither the reviewer nor anyone else needs a separate evidence decision before or after the verdict: the send-back or approval decides every awaiting piece of the task in the one action.
Approving a task while naming any of its pieces as failing is refused, naming the contradiction.

list_evidence, the task's history and the app's evidence views show each piece's outcome (accepted, rejected, held, awaiting) with its own reason and who decided it, and filtering by review state distinguishes held from rejected.
The review turn's brief and the update_task tool's description tell the reviewer how to name failing pieces and that unnamed ones are held, not rejected.

in_scope: A send-back naming failing pieces, each with its own reason, and an optional reason for the send-back as a whole
A third outcome for a piece on a send-back: held at that commit, neither accepted nor rejected
Held pieces recorded again at the builder's next commit and judged again
The per-piece outcome and reason in list_evidence, the task's history and today's evidence views
The reviewer's brief and the update_task tool saying how to name failing pieces
non_goals: Carrying held pieces forward to the next commit: deferred until roadmap slice H measures what re-recording costs (operator, 2026-10-26)
Rewriting past verdicts: evidence rejected in bulk before this ships stays as recorded
Per-model and per-level statistics: roadmap slice G reads what this records
The redesigned spec page's evidence display: slice F wires it
Changing approval: approving still accepts every awaiting piece of the task

summary: A reviewer's verdict stays one action, but inside it each piece of evidence gets its own outcome: a send-back rejects only the pieces named as failing, each with its own reason, and keeps the others as held at that commit; the builder's next commit records them all again for the reviewer. The record, the task's history and the evidence views then say which requirement failed and why, and counts of rejections stop multiplying rounds by requirements.

Test red first against master's all-rejected behaviour.
